title: Scott Bessent Is at War With Prices — and Prices Are Winning!
summary: Finance commentator argues the Treasury is fighting bond yields while the administration's tariffs, Iran war and immigration policy stoke the inflation that pushes yields up.

assertions.quote: A tariff is just a tax paid by Americans, not by Canadians. The importer who brings the part across the border pays it
They raise production costs, and they push consumer prices up.
you haven't punished a foreign rival, you've just made American-built cars dramatically more expensive to build and to buy
If investors think tariffs and retaliation and energy fights are going to keep inflation running closer to 4% than 2, they'll demand higher yields

verdicts.note: Nominal long yields embed expected inflation, so policies that raise expected inflation raise borrowing costs, though how much of the 2026 yield rise is tariff-driven is contested.

assertions.quote: Oil exports have been squeezed hard, and energy prices have climbed, which feeds straight back into the inflation
Inflation has been above the Fed's target for 5 years now.
the very inflation the administration's tariffs, immigration policy, and foreign policy are helping to stoke

verdicts.note: Tariff pass-through and the war-driven energy spike are well documented; the labor-supply effect of immigration curbs on prices is real but smaller and harder to measure.

On the tariff part only: tariffs added 2.9 points to twelve-month consumer goods inflation at the February 2026 peak, but their contribution is forecast to fall to about zero by August 2026 and turn negative, so by late 2026 tariffs raise the goods price level without adding to the inflation rate.
